high.title: Dollar-Won Rises Slightly on Fed Rate Hike Possibility, Closes at 1,517.40 Won
high.summary: The USD/KRW exchange rate closed at 1,517.40, up 11.30 won from the previous Seoul session close, showing a "strong early, weak late" pattern during overnight trading. The won initially strengthened on expectations of a US-Iran ceasefire but later weakened after Fed Governor Christopher Waller left the door open for future interest rate hikes. This development is significant for KRW traders as it demonstrates how geopolitical developments and Fed policy signals continue to drive volatility. The 1,517-1,518 level appears to be a key resistance zone, with the pair showing sensitivity to both Middle East developments and US monetary policy expectations. Traders should monitor ceasefire progress and Fed communications for directional cues.

high.title: National Growth Fund Sees Record Debut - 87% Subscription Rate on First Day
high.summary: Korea's National Participation Growth Fund achieved remarkable success on its launch day, with 87.1% of the 600 billion won ($507 million) annual target subscribed and 24 out of 25 institutions exhausting their online allocations within hours. This represents a significant capital flow development that could impact both equity markets and the KRW. The massive retail participation indicates strong domestic investment appetite, potentially reducing reliance on foreign inflows and providing support for Korean assets. The fund's focus on high-tech industries and domestic growth sectors aligns with government policy priorities and could drive sustained domestic demand for Korean equities, offering structural support for the KOSPI's continued rally toward 8,000.

medium.title: Internet Banks Maintain 30% Mid-to-Low Credit Lending Target
medium.summary: Korea's three internet banks maintained mid-to-low credit lending ratios above 30% in Q1, with Kakao Bank leading at 45.6% for new loans. This regulatory compliance indicates continued implementation of financial inclusion policies while maintaining credit quality standards. The stable lending patterns suggest manageable credit risk in the digital banking sector.

medium.title: Korea Expected to Post 3.0% Growth Despite Oil Price Headwinds
medium.summary: JPMorgan economist Park Seok-gil forecasts Korea's economy will achieve 3.0% growth this year, with semiconductor export strength offsetting rising oil price pressures. The analysis highlights tech sector tailwinds as the dominant factor, supporting the positive outlook for Korean equities and potentially providing fundamental support for the KRW through improved trade dynamics.

medium.title: US-Iran Close to Ceasefire Deal as Negotiations Progress
medium.summary: US and Iran are reportedly close to ending hostilities with differences limited to "wording" of certain provisions, according to Axios. Trump has scheduled calls with Middle East leaders and will decide on resuming military action by tomorrow. This development could significantly impact global risk sentiment and KRW direction, with successful agreement likely supporting risk-on flows.

medium.title: Domestic Equities Expected to Remain Positive in H2 on Corporate Earnings
medium.summary: Mirae Asset Securities projects continued positive momentum for Korean stocks in H2, driven by earnings growth and household fund flows. KOSPI operating profit is forecast at 901 trillion won for 2026 and 1,125 trillion won for 2027, with semiconductors expected to post 30%+ profit growth through 2027.
